key_insight: A residual-driven adaptive multilevel stochastic Galerkin FEM provably drives both its error estimator and the true approximation error to zero under the stated assumptions.
engineering_relevance: The method supports error-controlled simulation of elliptic PDEs with uncertain diffusion coefficients, relevant to engineering models with spatially varying material properties.
method: Construct a computable residual-based error estimator under a parametric saturation assumption.
Enforce K-compatibility so coupled finite element meshes have comparable sizes.
Use estimator reliability, stability, and reduction properties to establish adaptive convergence.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports convergence proofs and numerical experiments that illustrate and confirm the theoretical findings, without quantitative results.
watch_item: The guarantees rely on parametric saturation and K-compatible meshes, which constrain implementation and mesh adaptation.
paper_title: Convergence of an adaptive multilevel stochastic Galerkin FEM driven by a residual-based error estimator
